purpose: Cholestyramine is used to lower high cholesterol levels in your blood, which helps reduce your risk of heart disease. It may also be used to relieve itching caused by a liver condition where bile builds up in the body. Your doctor may prescribe it along with a healthy diet and exercise.
how_it_works: Your liver makes bile acids using cholesterol from your blood. Cholestyramine works by binding to these bile acids in your gut like a sponge, so they get removed from your body in your stool instead of being reabsorbed. Because your liver then needs more cholesterol to make new bile acids, it pulls extra cholesterol out of your blood, which lowers your cholesterol levels.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are digestive, including constipation, bloating, gas, stomach upset, nausea, and heartburn. Constipation is the most frequent complaint, especially when you first start taking it. Drinking plenty of water and eating fiber-rich foods can help.
warnings: Cholestyramine can interfere with the absorption of many other medications, so always take your other medicines either 1 hour before or 4 to 6 hours after taking this medication. It can also reduce absorption of fat-soluble vitamins like A, D, E, and K, so your doctor may monitor your vitamin levels. Do not use it if you have complete blockage of your bile ducts. Let your doctor know about all medications and supplements you take.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 1 packet or scoop (4 grams) mixed into water or juice, taken 1 to 2 times per day with meals. Your doctor may gradually increase your dose up to 6 packets or scoops per day if needed. Always mix the powder completely in at least 2 to 6 ounces of liquid before drinking — never swallow it dry.
